facts.text: Module-level client configuration is removed in v1. Bare module-level attribute assignments `openai.api_key = ...`, `openai.api_base = ...`, and `openai.organization = ...` no longer configure the client and must be replaced by constructing an explicit client object, e.g. `client = OpenAI(api_key=...)`.

All module-level namespaced call patterns of the form `openai.<Namespace>.create(...)` are removed in v1, along with the equivalent `.list(...)` and `.retrieve(...)` calls. Named examples: `openai.ChatCompletion.create(...)`, `openai.Completion.create(...)`, `openai.Embedding.create(...)`, `openai.Image.create(...)`, `openai.Moderation.create(...)`. These must migrate to client-based calls, e.g. `client.chat.completions.create(...)`.

The `openai.error` submodule is removed. Exception classes that used to live there (`openai.error.RateLimitError`, `openai.error.ServiceUnavailableError`, `openai.error.InvalidRequestError`, `openai.error.AuthenticationError`, etc.) now live at the top level of the `openai` package (e.g. `openai.RateLimitError`). Any reference to `openai.error.*` needs to change.

EXPLICIT NON-SCOPE: response-object access patterns are unaffected — whether code reads a response via dict-style (`response['choices']`) or attribute-style (`response.choices`) access, both remain valid and must NOT be flagged as breaking.

The three changes listed (module-level config assignment, module-level namespaced calls, `openai.error` submodule) are the ONLY confirmed breaking changes in this migration; anything not described is unaffected.

Affected sites include those reached indirectly through a repository's own helper functions, so call chains must be traced rather than only inspecting the entry-point file; each affected site should be reported with file path relative to repo root, line number, exact code snippet, and reason.
